officialChecks.method: HTTPS GET; read release table text
officialChecks.evidence: Latest Preview Agility SDK: 1.721.3-preview, 7/30/2026. Other features in 721: LinAlg VectorAccumulate; Addition to existing LinAlg support in SM 6.10 preview.
officialChecks.interpretation: Supports current preview wording as of retrieval, not a promise about all future releases. This is not the first-ever DirectX matrix experiment.

officialChecks.method: GitHub raw HTTPS GET; read header and introduction
officialChecks.evidence: Title: 0035 - Linear Algebra Matrix; status: Accepted; Planned Version: SM 6.10. Introduction describes the former SM 6.8 Wave Matrix experiment.
officialChecks.interpretation: Accepted proposal status does not mean a generally available SDK release.

officialChecks.method: Gitiles base64 document GET; read background and target API support
officialChecks.evidence: Large matrix-multiply operations can be decomposed into many matrix multiplies over small sub-blocks. Metal support since MSL 2.3; earlier HLSL WaveMatrices experimental feature later withdrawn.
officialChecks.caveat: Document also contains stale D3D no-support wording. For current Dawn implementation status use specific merged CLs, not that stale line. Feature is experimental, not universal standard WebGPU availability.

officialChecks.evidence: Official cooperative-matrix extension exists; supported shapes and types depend on the implementation.

officialChecks.method: Official PDF retrieved; historical statement cross-checked in Dawn target-API documentation
officialChecks.caveat: Do not repeat demo's earliest A13/2019 hardware date; feature-set boundaries differ. Screenplay intentionally makes no earliest Apple-generation claim.

ort.weightPrecision: INT4; subgroup path dequantizes before f16 matrix arithmetic
ort.dateNote: Exact acquisition day not separately specified. Screen shows report snapshot date.
ort.protocol: Report Section 5: median of three process launches, 3 reps after 1 warmup, graph capture enabled, 128 generated tokens; later controlled four-arm rerun reports <=3.1% largest prefill spread, one binary with runtime switch and verified kernel identities.
ort.environment: RX 7900 XTX, Ryzen 9 9950X, 62 GB RAM, Windows 11 Enterprise 10.0.26200; AMD package 26.10.07.02, Agility 1.721.3.0, DXC 1.10.2605.24 (report configuration).
ort.notClaimed: 82% full-generation speedup; official ORT release support; same GPU or baseline as native result; uniform gains across prompt sizes

claims.claim: On-device inference benefits from efficient matrix multiplication, especially transformer prefill.
claims.limit: Do not say all inference is compute-bound; decode often has different constraints.

claims.claim: C' = A x B + C; a subgroup cooperates on distributed matrix fragments.
claims.limit: Illustration grid sizes are not hardware capability claims.

claims.claim: NVIDIA, AMD, Intel and Apple GPU families have matrix-acceleration paths.
claims.limit: Not every GPU, datatype or API configuration; no common launch date and no earliest Apple generation asserted. Intel official page returned 403.

claims.claim: Vulkan cooperative matrices are exposed via extensions.
D3D12 LinAlg SM6.10 is preview as checked on 2026-10-05; DirectX had an earlier withdrawn matrix experiment.
claims.limit: No invented first release date or assertion that DirectX never had matrix work before LinAlg.

claims.claim: Our five specified Dawn fixes are merged upstream.
claims.limit: Exclude CL326715 from our count. Dawn feature remains experimental; not universal WebGPU availability.

claims.claim: Our experimental ORT integration adds subgroup-size control, AMD configuration work and a controlled A/B switch; upstreaming remains work in the report.
claims.limit: Report snapshot; no new ORT mainline audit and no claim the patches have merged.
Do not mix with earlier report values 2825 -> 5141 or the Vulkan paired run 3005 -> 5058.

claims.claim: Same rerun: full generation 1116 -> 1025ms (~8% shorter), decode nearly unchanged; 128-token prompt prefill regresses to 0.93x.
claims.limit: 128 input tokens in the regression is distinct from 128 generated tokens in the full-run setup.
